note: Main domestic cup + second cup (if any) + super cup for 21 UEFA associations. Where a season page was available the 2025-26 edition (or 2025/2026 calendar-year edition) was used; dates are first round to final. winner_berth names the competition; the exact qualifying round is only given when the cited source states it.

main_cup.name: Lithuanian Football Cup (LFF Taurė)
main_cup.participants: 50 clubs in 2025: 10 A Lyga, 11 I Lyga, 13 II Lyga, 9 III Lyga, 9 SFL. Round I is played by I/II/III Lyga and SFL clubs (4 byes); the 10 A Lyga clubs enter in the round of 32.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Conference League first qualifying round
main_cup.quote: The winners qualified for the 2026–27 UEFA Conference League first qualifying round on a sporting merit (subject to receiving an UEFA licence).
main_cup.note: Calendar-year season (Apr-Sep). Final is a single match at a neutral ground (2025: Central Stadium of Jonava). Winner also enters the Lithuanian Supercup.

super_cup.name: Lithuanian Supercup (LFF Supertaurė)
super_cup.entrants: A Lyga champions vs Lithuanian Cup winners (since 2016 the league runners-up if one club wins the double)
super_cup.quote: an annual football match contested between the champions of the previous A Lyga season and the holders of the Lithuanian Football Cup ... played at the beginning of the season
super_cup.note: Played shortly before the A Lyga season starts (Feb/Mar); venue moves between cities.

main_cup.name: Luxembourg Cup (Coupe de Luxembourg)
main_cup.participants: 100 clubs. 1./2./3. Division clubs start in the preliminary and first rounds; the 16 National Division and 16 Division of Honour clubs join in the second round, drawn away to lower-tier sides.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Conference League second qualifying round
main_cup.quote: The competition began on 3 September 2025 and ends with the final, played at the Stade de Luxembourg, in May 2026.
main_cup.note: Single final at the Stade de Luxembourg (neutral). Rounds: preliminary, 1st, 2nd, round of 32, round of 16, quarter-finals, semi-finals, final.

main_cup.name: Maltese FA Trophy
main_cup.participants: Preliminary round: Challenge League, Gozo First Division and National Amateur League semi-finalists (13 clubs get byes). Round of 32 adds the 12 Premier League clubs.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Conference League second qualifying round
main_cup.quote: Valletta FC won 2-1 over Gżira United Fc in the Final making them champions. They have earned a place in the second qualifying round of the 2026–27 UEFA Conference League.
main_cup.note: Infobox gives 6 December 2025 – 24 May 2026; the 2026 final match box is dated 23 May 2026. Single final at the National Stadium, Ta' Qali.

super_cup.name: Maltese Super Cup
super_cup.entrants: Premier League champions vs FA Trophy winners (league runners-up if one club wins both)
super_cup.quote: Up till 2003, the match used to be played at the end of the season, however, this was altered to be played around mid-December. The current holders are Valletta, who defeated Floriana 2–0 in the final played on the 7th of September.
super_cup.note: Source gives both 'mid-December' and a 7 September date for the current edition; treat the exact slot as unsettled.

main_cup.name: Moldovan Cup (Cupa Moldovei)
main_cup.participants: 37 clubs (2025-26), starting with a first preliminary round on 3 September.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Europa League first qualifying round
main_cup.quote: The competition started on 3 September 2025 with the first preliminary round and concluded with the final on 23 May 2026.
main_cup.note: Single final at the Zimbru Stadium, Chișinău.

super_cup.name: Moldovan Super Cup (Supercupa Moldovei)
super_cup.entrants: Liga champions vs Moldovan Cup winners
super_cup.quote: Over the course of 24 years, this match has been held 12 times. Eight times it was cancelled cause the same team won both the championship and the cup, and four times the Moldovan Football Federation decided not to hold the match.
super_cup.note: Irregular: held roughly every other year.

main_cup.name: Montenegrin Cup
main_cup.participants: 16 clubs (round of 16 as the first round).
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Conference League first qualifying round
main_cup.quote: The 2025–26 Montenegrin Cup was the 20th edition of the knockout football tournament in Montenegro, the tournament began on 22 October 2025.
main_cup.note: 16 clubs, the round of 16 drawn in mid-October is the first round. (The infobox match count of 17 does not match a plain 16-team bracket.)

main_cup.name: Macedonian Football Cup
main_cup.participants: 29 clubs (2025-26). The cited source does not break the field down by tier.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Conference League qualifying
main_cup.quote: The 2025–26 Macedonian Football Cup was the 34th season of North Macedonia's football knockout competition.
main_cup.note: Dates from the infobox (26 August 2025 – 20 May 2026). The cup article states no European round; it follows the UEFA access list (low-ranked association, Conference League qualifying).

main_cup.name: Irish Cup
main_cup.participants: All IFA senior and intermediate clubs. Four qualifying rounds (from August) reduce the level-3-and-below entrants to 8, who join the 24 NIFL Premiership/Championship clubs in a 32-club first round in January.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Conference League second qualifying round
main_cup.quote: The 2025–26 Irish Cup ... was the 146th edition of the Irish Cup, the premier knock-out cup competition in Northern Irish football since its inauguration in 1881. The winners qualified for the 2026–27 Conference League second qualifying round.
main_cup.note: Replays abolished from the whole competition in 2014; level ties go to extra time and penalties. Both semi-finals and the final are usually at Windsor Park. Berth passes to the 3rd-placed league club if the winner is already qualified or unlicensed.

second_cup.name: Northern Ireland Football League Cup (BetMcLean Cup)
second_cup.participants: 38 clubs — all member clubs of the Northern Ireland Football League (Premiership, Championship, Premier Intermediate), with a preliminary round.
second_cup.quote: The competition was contested by the 38 member clubs of the Northern Ireland Football League, commencing on 12 August 2025 with the preliminary round and concluding with the final on 15 March 2026.
second_cup.note: No European berth; secondary to the Irish Cup.

super_cup.name: NIFL Charity Shield
super_cup.entrants: NIFL Premiership champions vs Irish Cup winners
super_cup.quote: It pits together the previous campaign's NIFL Premiership champions and Irish Cup winners, providing the opening match of the Irish League season.
super_cup.note: Held on an occasional basis since 1992; 2025 edition won by Dungannon Swifts.

main_cup.name: Norwegian Football Cup (NM Cupen)
main_cup.participants: 80 clubs in the competition proper; 176 clubs from tiers 4-6 played two qualifying rounds (March-April) to send 44 into the first round. In 2025-26 the 16 Eliteserien clubs entered directly at the third round.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Europa League second qualifying round
main_cup.quote: It started on 13 August 2025, and ended with the final on 9 May 2026.
main_cup.note: 2025-26 was the first season of the new autumn-spring format (previously a calendar-year cup ending in Nov/Dec). Transitional entry: Eliteserien clubs joined at the third round, and the winner was due to play a Europa League play-off against the 2025 cup winner (cancelled as Bodø/Glimt won both). Final at Ullevaal Stadion.

main_cup.name: Polish Cup (Puchar Polski)
main_cup.participants: 70 clubs: 16 Ekstraklasa + 18 I liga + 18 II liga + 16 regional cup winners + 2 lower-placed I liga sides; the 4 UEFA-qualified clubs enter at the round of 32.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Europa League third qualifying round
main_cup.quote: The competition began on 5 August 2025 with the preliminary round and ended on 2 May 2026 with the final match at the Stadion Narodowy in Warsaw.
main_cup.note: Every tie is a single game at the lower-league club's ground; the final is a single match at the Stadion Narodowy since 2007 (two-legged finals were 2002-2006 only).

super_cup.name: Polish Super Cup (Superpuchar Polski)
super_cup.entrants: Ekstraklasa champions vs Polish Cup winners (cup runners-up if one club wins both)
super_cup.quote: Unlike the Polish Cup, there is no extra time played in the competition, therefore in case of a draw after regular time, the match goes straight into a penalty shoot-out.
super_cup.note: Played in July, before the Ekstraklasa season.

main_cup.name: FAI Cup
main_cup.participants: 44 clubs in 2026: League of Ireland Premier Division and First Division clubs plus clubs from the regional leagues.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Europa League first qualifying round
main_cup.quote: dates: 10 May – 8 November 2026
main_cup.note: Calendar-year season; first round in May, single final in November (Aviva Stadium). Rounds decided on the day by extra time and penalties.

super_cup.name: President of Ireland's Cup (President's Cup)
super_cup.entrants: League of Ireland Premier Division champions vs FAI Cup winners
super_cup.quote: It is a one-off match between the winners of the previous season's League of Ireland Premier Division and the FAI Cup, and functions both as a domestic Super cup and an unofficial opener to the football season in Ireland.

main_cup.name: Cupa României
main_cup.participants: 171 clubs: 42 in the regional/county qualifying competition and 136 in the main competition (incl. 7 qualifiers). County/regional stage, then national knockout rounds through a play-off round, a group stage of four groups (A-D), then quarter-finals, semi-finals and the final; Liga I clubs enter at the play-off/group stage.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Europa League first qualifying round
main_cup.quote: dates: 30 July 2025 – 13 May 2026
main_cup.note: Group stage = four groups (A-D) with the top two reaching the quarter-finals; in 2025-26 the quarter-finals and semi-finals were single legs, but the FRF may choose two legs for round of 16/quarter/semi in other years. Single final at a pre-established venue (normally Bucharest).

super_cup.name: Supercupa României
super_cup.entrants: Liga I champions vs Cupa României winners (league runners-up if one club wins both)
super_cup.quote: It is usually played at the Arena Națională in Bucharest.
super_cup.note: Played in July, before the Liga I season.

main_cup.name: Russian Cup
main_cup.participants: 104 clubs, split into an RPL path (the 16 Premier League clubs, group stage) and a regions path (knockout from the qualifying rounds).
main_cup.winner_berth: none
main_cup.quote: The winner of the cup would normally gain entry into the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League; however, on 28 February 2022, Russian football clubs were suspended from FIFA & UEFA international competitions until further notice.
main_cup.note: The final is a single match marketed as the 'Superfinal' (2026: Luzhniki, 24 May). Earlier editions (2010-11) used a two-legged final; not current.

super_cup.name: Russian Super Cup
super_cup.entrants: Russian Premier League champions vs Russian Cup winners (league runners-up if one club wins both)
super_cup.quote: The match is played at the beginning of the season, typically in July.

main_cup.name: Coppa Titano
main_cup.participants: 15 of the 16 Campionato Sammarinese clubs. The defending cup holders get a bye straight to the quarter-finals; the other 14 play a two-legged first round (round of 16).
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Conference League first qualifying round
main_cup.quote: The first legs were held on 23 and 24 September 2025, followed by the second legs on 20 and 21 October 2025.
main_cup.note: Only the final is a single match (23 May 2026, San Marino Stadium, Serravalle); the three earlier rounds are two-legged.

main_cup.name: Scottish Cup
main_cup.participants: 132 clubs in 2025-26 (entry open to all 134 full SFA members plus associates). Two preliminary rounds from 9 August; Highland/Lowland League (first round), League Two (second), Championship/League One (third), the 12 Premiership clubs (fourth round).
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Europa League qualifying (play-off round)
main_cup.quote: 9 August 2025 – 23 May 2026
main_cup.note: Dates from the season infobox and SFA calendar (preliminary round one 9 Aug 2025, final 23 May 2026 at Hampden Park). All ties decided on the day (extra time/penalties); no replays. The Scottish League Cup is the second cup and is covered in league-cups.json. The cup article does not state the European round — play-off round follows from Scotland's association ranking in the UEFA access list.

main_cup.name: Serbian Cup (Kup Srbije)
main_cup.participants: 36 clubs (2025-26); the cited source does not break the field down by tier.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Europa League qualifying
main_cup.quote: It started on 10 September 2025, and ended on 13 May 2026.
main_cup.note: Single final at a neutral ground (2026: Lagator Stadium, Loznica). Berth wording is the cup article's own ('a spot in the UEFA Europa League qualifying round'); the exact round follows the UEFA access list.

main_cup.name: Slovak Cup (Slovnaft Cup)
main_cup.participants: 292 clubs (2025-26) from all levels of the pyramid; the Fortuna Liga clubs join in the later rounds.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Europa League first qualifying round
main_cup.quote: The winners of the cup qualified for the 2026–27 UEFA Europa League first qualifying round.
main_cup.note: Dates from the infobox (18 July 2025 – 1 May 2026). Single final.

main_cup.name: Slovenian Football Cup (Pokal Slovenije)
main_cup.participants: Clubs from all tiers: regional (MNZ) preliminary, first and second rounds, then a 32-team national round of 32, round of 16, quarter-finals, semi-finals, final.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Europa League qualifying
main_cup.quote: Aluminij defeated second-division side Brinje Grosuplje 1–0 in the final and won its first major trophy
main_cup.note: No dates in the infobox. Earliest regional preliminary match listed is 9 August 2025; the national round of 32 was 21-30 October 2025; final 13 May 2026. Berth wording is competition-level only — the cup article states no round.

main_cup.name: Svenska Cupen
main_cup.participants: 96 clubs: 32 from Allsvenskan and Superettan plus 64 district qualifiers. Early knockout rounds in spring/summer, then a group stage in February-March before the quarter-finals.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Europa League first qualifying round
main_cup.quote: The 2025–26 Svenska Cupen was the 70th season of the Svenska Cupen and the 14th season in the current format ... A total of 96 clubs will compete in the competition, 64 teams from district sites and 32 from the Allsvenskan and the Superettan.
main_cup.note: Window spans 12 months: 7 May 2025 (first knockout rounds) to 14 May 2026 (final); group stage Feb-Mar 2026, quarter-finals/semi-finals/final in spring.

main_cup.name: Swiss Cup (Schweizer Cup)
main_cup.participants: 64 clubs: the 12 Super League clubs plus Challenge League, Promotion League and lower/regional qualifiers; Super League sides enter in the later rounds.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Europa League qualifying
main_cup.quote: 15 August 2025 – 24 May 2026
main_cup.note: Single final at the Wankdorf, Bern. The cup article states no European round; competition-level berth only.

main_cup.name: Ukrainian Cup
main_cup.participants: 68 clubs: a qualification round in early August, then a round of 64; Premier League clubs enter the later rounds.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Europa League first qualifying round
main_cup.quote: The competition started on 9 August 2025 and was concluded with the final on 20 May 2026 in Lviv.
main_cup.note: Infobox gives 8 August 2025 (qualification round 8-10 August). Single final in Lviv (neutral); wartime venue restrictions apply to eastern clubs.

super_cup.name: Ukrainian Super Cup
super_cup.entrants: Ukrainian Premier League champions vs Ukrainian Cup winners
super_cup.quote: Following the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the competition has been suspended.
super_cup.note: Season opener (July/August) while active; suspended since 2022.

main_cup.name: Welsh Cup (JD Welsh Cup)
main_cup.participants: Clubs from the third tier and below enter the first qualifying round, drawn geographically (100 northern + 128 southern clubs in 2025-26); Cymru Premier clubs join in the later rounds.
main_cup.winner_berth: UEFA Conference League first qualifying round
main_cup.quote: Matches were played on the weekend of 26 July 2025.
main_cup.note: First qualifying round ties on 25-27 July 2025; final 12 April 2026 at Rodney Parade, Newport (neutral). Round structure: 1st/2nd qualifying, 1st/2nd/3rd/4th round, quarter-finals, semi-finals, final. Welsh clubs playing in the English pyramid are excluded. The Welsh League Cup is the second cup and is covered in league-cups.json.
